curation.lead:
Carlos Ghosn is the former Nissan chair whose Japanese criminal proceedings prompted the U.S. advocacy documented here; Paul Weiss terminated its federal lobbying registration for him on February 25, 2020 [Finding #13195][Finding #13080]. His documentary relevance is the intersection between that formal Paul Weiss mandate and private Ghosn-related exchanges between firm chair Brad Karp and Jeffrey Epstein [Finding #13080][Finding #13075]. Seven Senate Lobbying Disclosure Act filings list Karp as a Paul Weiss lobbyist for Ghosn from the fourth quarter of 2018 through the February 2020 termination, describing advocacy with the media and U.S. government concerning reasonable bail and a fair trial in Japan [Finding #13080]. Karp's first surviving message saying he was “dealing with Ghosn crisis” is dated November 20, 2018, the same effective date shown on the federal registration [Finding #13164].

Epstein subsequently offered Karp “gchosen info”; Karp replied that the offer was quick, that he was on a DOJ call, and that he would call immediately afterward [Finding #13075]. After returning from Tokyo, Karp told Epstein, “Your guy totally had it right,” and Epstein later offered to update him on “google. ghosen SIC and ...” [Finding #13075]. These exchanges document offered and shared Ghosn-related information, but they do not establish whether it was public or private, identify the source, prove client authorization, or show that Paul Weiss used it in Ghosn's representation [Finding #13075][Finding #13203][Finding #13213].

sections.title: The Paul Weiss Mandate
sections.content:
The federal lobbying registration for Carlos Ghosn Bichara became effective on November 20, 2018 and listed Brad Karp among the new lobbyists for Paul Weiss [Finding #13164]. Seven filings cover the 2018 fourth quarter through a February 25, 2020 termination and describe work directed at media and U.S. government audiences concerning bail and a fair trial in Japan [Finding #13080]. The filings report firm-client income of $20,000 for the 2018 fourth quarter, $50,000 in each quarter of 2019, and $20,000 in the 2020 first quarter, totaling $240,000; those figures are not Karp's personal compensation [Finding #13080].

Paul Weiss states that Karp, Michael Gertzman, and Kaye Yoshino led the team for Ghosn's September 23, 2019 SEC settlement, with Daniel Juceam and Chikara Momota also participating [Finding #13195]. The SEC said Ghosn agreed to a $1 million civil penalty and a ten-year officer-and-director bar without admitting or denying the allegations [Finding #13195]. No located source traces information supplied by Jeffrey Epstein into that settlement or any other downstream work for Ghosn [Finding #13195][Finding #13213].

sections.title: The Karp–Epstein Ghosn Exchanges
sections.content:
On November 20, 2018, Karp told Epstein he was “dealing with Ghosn crisis,” matching the effective date of the public Ghosn lobbying registration [Finding #13164]. On November 30, Epstein asked Tom Pritzker to ask around about Ghosn's incommunicado detention; Pritzker replied only that the situation was “weird” and that he would see [Finding #13203]. Thirty-two minutes after Pritzker's reply, Epstein offered Karp “gchosen info,” and Karp answered that the offer was quick, that he was on a DOJ call, and that he would call immediately afterward [Finding #13203][Finding #13075]. The wording does not establish that the DOJ call concerned Ghosn [Finding #13075].

On December 26, Epstein asked Karp for updates and wrote that “my guy had it right from day one” [Finding #13203]. Karp replied while returning from Tokyo, “Your guy totally had it right” [Finding #13075][Finding #13203]. On January 24, 2019, Epstein offered to bring Karp up to date on “google. ghosen SIC and ...,” and Karp agreed before Epstein supplied a French telephone number [Finding #13075][EFTA02626768]. On January 26, Epstein called Ghosn “a very very not good guy,” and Karp replied “Indeed” [EFTA02627328][EFTA02627279].

sections.title: Source Attribution and Evidentiary Limits
sections.content:
Tom Pritzker is the only named, temporally proximate upstream-source candidate located in the November 30 sequence, but his preserved response contains no substantive Ghosn information and does not prove that he was Epstein's later “my guy” [Finding #13203]. The January 2019 context favors “Senate Intelligence Committee” as the meaning of “SIC” and treats it as a separate update topic from Ghosn, although the acronym is never explicitly expanded in the released messages [Finding #13197]. The French telephone number supplied after the January 24 exchange does not by itself identify a caller, source, meeting, or Ghosn-related purpose [EFTA02626768].

In the same January 26 exchange, Epstein asked whether Karp represented Rajeev Misra, an executive associated with SoftBank, and Karp replied, “Sort of. Spoke to him yesterday” [Finding #832][EFTA02627034][EFTA02627134]. The released message does not tie the Misra question to Ghosn, so it is logged as an adjacent contact rather than evidence about the source or use of Ghosn information [Finding #832].

The surviving Ghosn messages establish episodic, matter-centered contact between Karp and Epstein [Finding #13213]. They do not show whether the offered information was public, privileged, accurate, client-authorized, relayed to Ghosn's defense team, or used in later advocacy or litigation [Finding #13075][Finding #13213].

curation.system_role: Subject of a documented 2018–2020 Paul Weiss mandate whose matter also appeared in private Karp–Epstein information exchanges [Finding #13080][Finding #13075]. The record proves the exchanges and the public mandate, but not the information's status, authorization, downstream use, or effect [Finding #13213].
open_questions: What source produced the Ghosn assessment that Epstein and Karp later described as having been right from day one, and do full headers or adjacent messages narrow the candidates beyond the bounded Pritzker sequence [Finding #13203]?
Does any released attachment, call memorandum, or follow-up message preserve the substance of the “gchosen info” Epstein offered Karp on November 30, 2018 [Finding #13075][Finding #13203]?
Do Paul Weiss matter files, billing narratives, interview notes, or privilege logs show whether any Epstein-supplied information entered the Ghosn representation [Finding #13213]?
Who used the French telephone number supplied after the January 24 update offer, and was the number connected to Ghosn or to one of the separately listed topics [EFTA02626768][Finding #13197]?
Did Ghosn or another authorized member of his team know about or approve Karp's Ghosn-related exchanges with Epstein [Finding #13075]?

citation_findings.summary: New surveillance, billing, specialist-counsel, and Ghosn evidence strengthens a narrow matter-specific reciprocity conclusion without establishing a durable systematic symbiosis. Karp relayed concrete surveillance status and movement information to Epstein, while Epstein comments entered Black tax drafting and Epstein offered Ghosn information; however the located Paul Weiss billing lacks timekeeper allocation, specialist counsel handled other technical work, and no source traces Epstein information into the later Ghosn settlement. The best-supported model remains episodic client-centered contact with pockets of two-way professional assistance.
citation_findings.detail: This synthesis treats the Black surveillance, Nardello, Forms 8865, fee, and billing records as one client-centered evidence cluster rather than separate votes. The Ghosn information offer, Pritzker timing, Tokyo reply, and SEC outcome are likewise one sequence. It does not infer the surveillance client, payer, investigator, authorization, or outcome; it does not claim that Epstein information was nonpublic or used; and it does not claim that no unlocated compensation or engagement record exists.
citation_findings.target_name: Brad S. Karp and Jeffrey Epstein relationship model
